d: A Colombian platter bringing together beans, rice, meat, crispy pork, egg, plantain and avocado.
s: Reheat the beans with some of the onion and tomato.
Cook the ground beef with the rest of the onion and tomato.
Cook the pork belly until crispy.
Brown the plantains and fry the eggs sunny side up.
Arrange all the components on large plates.

d: Goat or chicken marinated with tamarind and spices, cooked inside bamboo stalks over the fire; adapted here as a foil packet.
s: Pound the shallots, garlic, lemongrass, chilies and turmeric into a paste.
Marinate the meat with the paste, tamarind, basil and salt for 1 hour.
Pack the meat into bamboo sections or a tightly sealed foil packet.
Cook for 1 hour 30 minutes over embers or in the oven at 170 °C.
Serve with rice.

d: Fish poached in a fragrant broth with cassava, sweet potato, green banana and cabbage.
s: Sauté the onion, garlic and tomatoes in the oil.
Add 2 liters of water and the vegetables; cook 20 minutes.
Add the salted fish and poach 10 to 12 minutes.
Lift the fish and vegetables onto a platter.
Serve with the broth on the side, thickened with a little cornmeal if desired.

d: Lamb braised with tomato and cinnamon, then baked with kritharaki pasta in a clay dish and served with grated cheese.
s: Brown the lamb in the oil, then add the onion and garlic.
Deglaze with the wine; add the tomatoes, cinnamon, salt and pepper.
Transfer to a clay baking dish, cover and bake 1 hour 30 minutes at 180 °C.
Add the orzo and 1 L of boiling water; stir.
Bake 30 minutes more, uncovered, stirring once.
Serve sprinkled with grated cheese.

d: A white bean, onion and parsley salad from the Turkish and Persian tradition; this version skips the tahini dressing.
s: Rinse and drain the cooked beans thoroughly.
Slice the onion very thinly. Rub it with salt and sumac and let it rest 5 minutes.
Dice the tomatoes and chop the parsley. Combine with the beans and onion.
Add the oil and vinegar, toss gently and let rest 15 minutes before serving.

d: Green plantain rounds fried, flattened, then fried again until crisp, salted and served with a garlic mojo.
s: Peel the plantains and cut them into 3 cm pieces.
Fry 4 minutes at 160 °C without browning; drain.
Flatten each piece with a tostonera or the bottom of a glass.
Fry again at 180 °C until golden, drain and salt.
Serve with a mojo of crushed garlic, citrus juice and warm oil.

d: Minced chicken cooked with tomatoes, onions, garlic, ginger and chilies, served with Bhutanese red rice.
s: Put the chicken in a saucepan with 300 ml of water and the oil.
Add the onion, garlic, ginger and chilies; cook 15 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook 10 minutes.
Season with salt, sprinkle with cilantro and serve with red rice.

d: Fried potato cubes served with a spicy paprika brava sauce, a tapa born in the bars of Madrid.
s: Gently poach the potatoes in the oil at 140 °C for 15 minutes.
Drain, then fry at 180 °C until crisp.
For the sauce, sauté the garlic in 2 tablespoons of oil and stir in the flour.
Off the heat, add both paprikas, then whisk in the stock.
Cook 5 minutes; add the vinegar and salt.
Salt the potatoes and top with the brava sauce.

d: Flour dumplings poached, then served with bacon, brown butter and cream — a Luxembourg family classic.
s: Mix the flour, eggs, milk, salt and nutmeg into a thick, smooth batter.
Scoop dumplings with a spoon and poach them in salted water until they float.
Brown the bacon, then add the butter.
Toss the drained dumplings with the bacon and butter.
Serve with a drizzle of cream and applesauce.

d: A golden soufflé shaped into three peaks that recall the snowy mountains around Salzburg, baked over lingonberry jam and dusted with icing sugar.
s: Preheat the oven to 220 °C.
Butter an oval dish, spread the jam in it and pour in the milk.
Beat the egg whites with the sugar to stiff peaks.
Gently fold in the yolks, zest, vanilla and then the sifted flour.
Shape 3 large peaks in the dish with a spatula.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes; dust with icing sugar and serve immediately.

d: Raw butterflied shrimp quickly “cooked” in lime juice blended with serrano or chiltepín chilies, with cucumber and red onion.
s: Salt the shrimp and lay them flat in a shallow dish.
Blend the lime juice, chilies, cilantro and salt.
Pour over the shrimp.
Add the cucumber and red onion.
Let rest 10 minutes in the fridge until the shrimp turn opaque.
Serve right away with tostadas.

d: Small pleated dumplings steamed in bamboo baskets, filled with pork and jellied broth that melts as they cook; born in Nanxiang near Shanghai.
s: The day before, make a reduced pork-skin broth that sets into jelly.
Mix the pork, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, ginger, sesame oil and sugar; fold in the diced jelly.
Knead the flour and water; rest 30 minutes.
Divide into 10 g balls and roll into discs that are thin at the edges.
Fill and pleat with about 18 folds.
Steam 8 minutes on parchment or cabbage leaves; serve with ginger black vinegar.

d: A Bengali sweet: chhena (fresh cheese curdled with lemon) kneaded until smooth, shaped into balls and cooked in light syrup, where they swell and turn spongy.
s: Bring the milk to a boil and add the lemon to curdle it; drain the chhena in muslin, rinse and hang for 45 minutes.
Knead the chhena 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and slightly greasy.
Shape 14 balls with no cracks.
Bring the water, sugar and cardamom to a boil and drop in the balls; cover and cook 15 minutes at a rolling boil.
Let cool in the syrup, flavor with rose water and serve chilled.

d: A clear beef broth with liver, bread and marjoram dumplings — a classic starter in Liechtenstein inns.
s: Squeeze the bread and mix it with the liver, egg, onion, herbs, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper.
Let rest 20 minutes.
Shape dumplings with wet hands.
Poach them 20 minutes in simmering broth.
Serve in the broth with chives.

d: Soft yeasted oat and wheat pancakes, a Staffordshire specialty quite different from Scottish oatcakes.
s: Mix the flours, yeast and salt. Whisk in the warm milk and water to make a pancake batter.
Cover and let ferment about 1 hour at room temperature, until small bubbles form.
Lightly oil a hot pan. Pour in a ladleful and spread into a thin pancake.
Cook 2 minutes, then flip for 1 minute. Fill with cheese or cooked bacon if you like and fold over.

d: A fine meat sauce spiced with cinnamon, cocoa and cloves, served over spaghetti under a mountain of shredded cheddar — created by Macedonian immigrants in Cincinnati.
s: Break up the raw beef in cold water (do not brown it).
Add the onion, tomato paste, spices, cocoa and vinegar.
Simmer 2 hours uncovered until the sauce is loose but coats a spoon.
Skim off the fat and season with salt.
Cook the spaghetti.
Serve spaghetti, then chili, then a mountain of cheddar (three-way).

d: Fried yeasted bread rolls, split and filled with curried ground beef, hugely popular in Namibia.
s: Knead the flour, yeast, sugar, 1 tsp salt and water; let rise 1 hour.
Cook the meat with the onion, curry powder and tomato for 20 minutes; season with salt.
Shape the dough into balls and let rest 10 minutes.
Fry 5 minutes at 170 °C, turning.
Split the vetkoek and fill with the meat.

d: An Angolan stew of dried or fresh fish with leafy greens, tomato, okra and palm oil.
s: Sauté the onion and garlic in the palm oil.
Add the tomatoes and okra and cook 8 minutes.
Add the smoked fish, then the greens and 250 ml of water.
Lay the fresh fish on top and cover.
Simmer gently 25 to 30 minutes without stirring too much.

d: Little balls of sweet yeasted dough fried until puffy and golden — a party and street snack in Lagos.
s: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast, nutmeg and salt.
Add the warm water and beat into a thick, sticky batter.
Cover and let rise 1 hour.
Heat the oil to 170 °C.
Grab some batter and squeeze it out between thumb and forefinger into balls in the oil.
Fry, turning, until golden; drain.

d: Korean pork gently boiled then sliced, served with lettuce leaves, kimchi and ssamjang.
s: Put the water, doenjang, garlic, ginger, cut onion and peppercorns in a pot and bring to a simmer.
Add the pork and cook at a gentle simmer for 60 to 75 minutes, turning if needed.
Check that the pork is tender and reaches at least 71 °C. Remove and rest 10 minutes before slicing.
Wash the lettuce leaves and set out the kimchi and ssamjang in small bowls.
Slice the pork ¼ inch thick. At the table, wrap a slice and a little of the condiments in a leaf; serve right away.
